_doc: [pace2] Leave early, come back later: tech = tools found on later planets (granted when that planet's restoration reaches `at`); a planet's needs_tech [[tech, cap], ...] caps its restoration at cap until the tech is found, so 100% needs return trips. Research nodes take requires_tech. Drives open from partial progress (requires_planet_pct [k, pct], requires_other_pct). [v6pace] planets[k].leave = that planet's own gate for moving on (owner note 58: not tied to cleaning the planet): hubs + hub_level = that many hubs there restored to that base level open the system and the next drive (owner note 61; Homeward.hubs_at_level); or base_level = one base at that level (replaces the drive's or_base_level for that planet); toast = what WREN says the moment it opens. [home] Homeward: the campaign across the Verdance system (systems/homeward.gd). Five fixed planets in order (profile worlds; planet 0 = Verdance = world 0). A planet's restoration (0..1): Verdance = its Bloom Core charge (100% when the Cradle answers); other planets = w_thriving * min(1, thriving hexes / thriving) + w_bases * min(1, bases at level 5 / bases) + w_start * min(1, start-district Thriving share / start_ratio). It never drops (best value kept in the profile). System restoration = mean over the five. A restored planet (100%) gives its relic and one Heirloom pick. Drive tiers (Mk V-VII) are the rocket's interplanetary drive, kept in the profile and carried to every planet: a planet needs drive >= nav and its chart (the previous planet at chart_at). [v7arc] Mk VII needs requires_home: the home meters full (data/story_arc.json: fuel and power from every planet's exit beat), and Lumi at Verdance's Cradle Returns. requires_relics / requires_system (N relics, whole system restored) still work as drive gates but are no longer used: every planet at 100% is an optional extra (relics, Heirloom picks, the restored notes, and the greener Homecoming). Costs: cubes and parts.

planets.name: Verdance

leave.toast: Six stations awake, Lumi. Their robots can look after Verdance now.

planets.twist: Home. The Settlers' world, buried under the Ledger's trash. Your robots keep cleaning it while you are away.

planets.name: Ochre
planets.twist: The Ledger's first strip mine: open pits and slag dunes. Rich salvage, steady wind, very little water.

planets.name: Tidewell
planets.twist: An ocean the dredgers drained of minerals. Towns on islands, rain every hour, life desperate to come back.

planets.name: Rime
planets.twist: A moon core-mined until its heat ran out and it froze. Long nights, thin soil, lakes under the ice.

planets.name: Anvil
planets.twist: The Ledger's foundry world and head office. Pole-to-pole rust, the heaviest scrap in the system, and a hollow core.

tech.name: Deep Drill
tech.desc: Ochre's miners bored through bedrock. On Verdance it breaks open the buried landfill of the Dust Flats.

tech.name: Tide Pump
tech.desc: Tidewell's sea pumps. On Verdance they drain the flooded streets of the Sunken City.

tech.name: Cryo Beacon
tech.desc: A beacon that sings through deep cold: what Verdance's Ark Beacon was missing.

tech.name: Heat Core
tech.desc: Anvil's forge heart. Wound into the beam, it melts the Frozen Port's ice on Verdance.

ochre_glass.name: Ochre Sun-Glass
ochre_glass.desc: Slag fused clear by the dune winds. It holds a little of Ochre's light.

tidewell_pearl.name: Tidewell Pearl
tidewell_pearl.desc: The first pearl grown in Tidewell's sea in two hundred years.

rime_core.name: Rime Heart-Ice
rime_core.desc: A core sample from the thawed lakes, still faintly warm.

anvil_ingot.name: Anvil Ingot
anvil_ingot.desc: The Ledger's last ingot, recast as a plain ring with a seed stamped in it.

drive.name: Mk V Orbital
drive.desc: Your hop rocket, rebuilt for space out of a mountain of cubes. It reaches the near planets, Ochre and Tidewell.

drive.name: Mk VI Interplanetary
drive.desc: A fold drive salvaged from a Ledger ore hauler: reaches Rime and Anvil.

drive.name: Mk VII Homeward
drive.desc: A great green-light rocket, filled with the fuel and power of every world you woke. One trip: up to the Cradle.

ochre_arrive.header: L E D G E R   ·   I N T E R N A L
ochre_arrive.title: Site closure notice, Ochre Open Pit 1
ochre_arrive.body:
OCHRE OPEN PIT 1: CLOSED

Ore grade below threshold. All extraction ends at shift change.
Remaining equipment: abandon in place (removal not cost-effective).
Waste rock, slag and packaging: leave on site.
Residents: none of our concern; contracts expired.

Thank you for your years of service.
— The Ledger

ochre_half.title: Haul truck log, unit OH-7
ochre_half.body:
DAY 1,904
Load 41 to the slag dunes.
DAY 1,905
No orders.
DAY 1,906
No orders.
DAY 3,000
Still parked. The wind keeps burying my wheels. A lizard lives under my bumper now. I have named it Load 42.

ochre_restored.title: Chalk on a pit wall
ochre_restored.body:
[In big careful letters, on the old benches of the pit:]

THE GREEN CAME BACK.

[Underneath, smaller, in WREN's handwriting font:] One down, Lumi. Four to go.

tidewell_arrive.header: L E D G E R   ·   I N T E R N A L
tidewell_arrive.title: Dredging schedule, final revision
tidewell_arrive.body:
TIDEWELL SEABED OPERATIONS

Nodules recovered: 100%.
Reef and kelp beds: 'overburden', removed.
Silt plumes: within acceptable limits (limits revised).
Island towns: notified by post.

Next quarter: none. Tidewell is closed for business.

tidewell_half.title: Harbour radio, on a loop
tidewell_half.body: ...this is Tidewell harbour, still broadcasting. The water's gone grey and the fish have gone quiet. If anyone hears this, we planted mangroves along the north quay before we left. Check on them for us? They were only little...

tidewell_restored.title: A message in a bottle
tidewell_restored.body:
To whoever finds this,

The sea used to be so green you could see it from the hill. Grandad said it would come back if someone gave it a reason.

Thank you for being the reason.

— Pim, age 9, Tidewell

rime_arrive.header: L E D G E R   ·   I N T E R N A L
rime_arrive.title: Core tap report, Rime
rime_arrive.body:
RIME DEEP CORE TAP

Heat extracted and sold: all of it.
Surface temperature: falling (expected).
Lakes: freezing (expected).
Population: relocated (see invoice).

Note from Finance: the moon was not ours to keep warm.

rime_half.title: Greenhouse keeper's diary
rime_half.body:
Day 1. The heaters are off. Moved the seedlings to the kitchen.
Day 9. Kitchen's cold too. Wrapped them in my coat.
Day 30. We're leaving on the last shuttle. I left the coat. And a note: please keep them warm. I know that's silly. You're a frozen moon.

rime_restored.title: A note pinned in a thawed greenhouse
rime_restored.body:
[Under the note from Day 30, a new line in bright ink:]

Kept them warm. They're fine. They're more than fine.

— LM-1 (and WREN, who wants it known she helped)

anvil_arrive.header: L E D G E R   ·   H E A D   O F F I C E
anvil_arrive.title: Board minutes, the final meeting
anvil_arrive.body:
ITEM 1: The system is spent. Motion to dissolve: carried.
ITEM 2: Clean-up costs. Motion to not: carried.
ITEM 3: The Settlers' ark keeps asking about a 'charter'. Motion to ignore: carried.
ITEM 4: Audit drones to continue indefinitely, for form's sake.

Meeting closed. Lights left on.

anvil_half.title: The last audit
anvil_half.body:
LEDGER AUDIT UNIT 0001
SUBJECT: Anvil foundry district
FINDING: Unauthorised gardens. 214 counts.
FINDING: Unauthorised gardens. 215 counts.
FINDING: ...
RECOMMENDATION: Recommend we stop counting. It is rather nice.

anvil_restored.title: From the Ledger's last clerk
anvil_restored.body:
Whoever you are,

I kept the books for forty years. I wrote down every ton we took. I never wrote down what we left.

If you're reading this in a garden on Anvil, then someone finally balanced the account. Thank you.

— T. Hale, Accounts
